events.content: Super Micro Computer AI server revenue Q1 fiscal 2027 net sales guidance

Super Micro Computer’s quarter ended **September 30, 2025** was **Q1 fiscal 2026—not Q1 fiscal 2027**; the company reported total net sales of **$5.018 billion**. [[1]] 

Management said that **AI GPU platforms accounted for more than 75% of Q1 revenue**, implying AI-server/platform revenue of **more than approximately $3.76 billion** ($5.018 billion × 75%). [[2]] [[1]] 

This is an inferred lower bound rather than a separately disclosed “AI server revenue” line item: Supermicro’s reported financial statements disclose consolidated net sales, while the AI-platform figure was stated as a revenue mix percentage. [[1]] [[2]]

Sources:

tool_arguments.query: Super Micro Computer latest revenue guidance fiscal 2026 or fiscal 2027

events.content: Super Micro Computer latest revenue guidance fiscal 2026 or fiscal 2027

Super Micro Computer (SMCI) did **not separately disclose an “AI server revenue” dollar line item** in its Q3 fiscal 2026 release; therefore, the reported company-wide net-sales figure is the definitive quarterly revenue measure. [[1]] 

For the fiscal third quarter ended **March 31, 2026**, Supermicro reported net sales of **$10.243 billion**, up **123% year over year** from **$4.600 billion** in Q3 FY2025 and down about **19% sequentially** from **$12.7 billion** in Q2 FY2026. [[1]] 

AI-related platforms reportedly represented **more than 90% of revenue in recent quarters**, which would imply an AI-platform revenue run rate of **more than roughly $9.2 billion** when applied to Q3’s $10.243 billion total; however, that is an inference rather than a company-reported Q3 AI-server-revenue figure. [[2]] [[1]] 

Other Q3 FY2026 results were **GAAP net income of $483 million**, **GAAP diluted EPS of $0.72**, **non-GAAP diluted EPS of $0.84**, and **GAAP gross margin of 9.9%**. [[1]] 

Management attributed the quarterly revenue shortfall versus its prior quarter to customer data-center/site-readiness delays and industry-wide supply constraints, while indicating that it expected delayed revenue to be recognized in subsequent quarters. [[3]] [[4]] 

For Q4 FY2026, Supermicro guided to **$11.0 billion–$12.5 billion** of net sales and maintained FY2026 net-sales guidance of **$38.9 billion–$40.4 billion**. [[1]]

Sources:
